label: Shadows Veil
line: Shadows Veil — neon on brick, incense on rain.
bible:
Shadows Veil is where the veil runs thin. Humans hold most of the counters and chancery steps; demons fix the streetlamps beside them, angels walk the night watch, and vampires keep honest jobs and drink bottled vitae like anyone else's supper.

Magic is uncommon but not secret. Threshold signs chalked over doors, dead fixtures coaxed back to light, small courtesies traded across counters — the streets have seen it all and mostly nod along. Nobody duels in the square; signs are for homes and jobs, not wars.

Two institutions hold the line. The parish keeps the rites, rations out the vitae for those who thirst, and marries whoever asks. The night market moves everything else: dry goods, grid charges, bottled drinks under the counter, gossip by the pound.

What the city knows about anyone is common talk. What they keep in the back rooms — fears, appetites, the exact terms of an old vow — stays theirs unless they choose to say it.
